messages.text: I'm a full-time college student at MTSU and broke. Can I get food stamps?

Maybe. College students have extra rules for food assistance (SNAP), so I need a few details first.

1. Who lives with you and shares food? Please give their ages. Also tell me if anyone is pregnant or has a disability.
2. Do you have any income before taxes, such as a job, financial aid paid to you, or help from family? If so, how much is it, and how often are you paid?

Just me, no one else in the apartment. Not pregnant, not disabled.

I work about 10 hours a week, around $500 a month before taxes. I'm paid monthly. I don't think I get any other income, not from family or anything like that.

Thanks, that helps. Two more questions:

1. How old are you?
2. How much is your monthly rent? Do you pay separately for heating or cooling (like an electric bill for AC or heat), for other utilities only, or is everything included in your rent?
I'm 20. Rent is $600 and utilities are included, so I don't pay anything extra for heat or AC.

A caseworker needs to look at your case. Being a full-time student makes it harder to get food assistance (SNAP), but you can still apply.

**Why it's a "caseworker needs to look" result**
- SNAP is generally closed to students ages 18 to 49 who are in college at least half time, unless they meet an exemption. USDA says: "Generally, students ages 18 through 49 who are enrolled in college at least half time are not eligible for SNAP unless they meet certain specific exemptions." ([USDA SNAP Eligibility](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/recipient/eligibility))
- Common exemptions include working 20 hours a week or caring for a young child. At about 10 hours a week, you probably don't meet the work one. I can't tell whether you meet any other exemption. Tennessee's rules are in [SNAP Policy 24.27, Students in Higher Education](https://www.tn.gov/content/dam/tn/human-services/documents/Policy%2024.27%20SNAP%20Students%20in%20Higher%20Educ.pdf).
- Ask the caseworker about other exemptions. One you might check is whether you're in a work-study program.

**Your income and size**
- Your income of $500 a month is well under the limits for a household of one: $1,729 before taxes and $1,330 after deductions. ([USDA's FY 2027 limits](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/allotment/cola))
- If the student rule weren't a problem, the screening says you'd likely qualify, with an estimated benefit of about $306 a month. That's only an estimate. It doesn't apply unless you meet an exemption.

**Other things to know**
- SNAP has a savings limit of $3,000 in cash and bank accounts. I haven't asked about your savings.
- Adults without children can have time limits on SNAP unless they work or train 20 hours a week. These rules changed in 2025, and the caseworker can explain what applies to you.

**TennCare:** It looks unlikely. Tennessee generally doesn't cover adults 19 to 64 who aren't pregnant, disabled, caring for a child, or former foster youth. You can still apply. ([TennCare Eligibility Reference Guide](https://www.tn.gov/coverkids/coverkids/redirect-income-guidelines.html))

**WIC:** This doesn't apply, because WIC is for pregnant women, new mothers, babies, and children under 5.

**How to apply**
- **SNAP:** Apply online through [OneDHS](https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp?id=start_snap_application) or call 866-311-4287.
- **TennCare:** Apply at [TennCare Connect](https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov/) or call 855-259-0701.
- **Free local help:** Dial 211.

This is a screening, not a decision. Only the state agency decides, and anyone can apply. Give accurate information on the application, including your school status and work hours. Overpayments have to be paid back.

Do you already get SNAP, WIC, or TennCare? Do you have a work-study job through MTSU? Either answer could change what to do next.

Do I have to pay the food stamps back if I get them and then find out I'm not allowed? And do I still have to work the 10 hours or can I quit? I'm not really sure yet what I'd even do about the student thing. I don't have a work-study job, I don't think. I don't get SNAP, WIC, or TennCare right now.

**Do you have to pay it back?**
Yes, you could. The policy search didn't return a Tennessee rule that spells out repayment, so I can't quote one. Overpayments, meaning benefits you got but weren't allowed, generally have to be paid back. That's why it matters to answer the application questions accurately, including that you're a student and how many hours you work. If you tell the caseworker everything and they approve you, that's the agency's decision based on what you told them. For questions about your own case, call 866-311-4287 or dial 211.

**Do you have to keep working 10 hours?**
I can't tell you whether to keep your job. That's your call. Here is what the official policy says:
- **Tennessee's "voluntary quit" rule** covers people who quit a job of 30 or more hours a week, or cut their hours to under 30. Your job is about 10 hours, so that rule doesn't look like it applies to you. A caseworker makes that call. ([TN DHS SNAP Policy 24.11](https://www.tn.gov/content/dam/tn/human-services/documents/24.11_SNAP_Work_Requirements_-_Esigned_unlined.pdf))
- **Your job doesn't meet the student exemption.** To qualify as a student, you'd need to be "employed an average of twenty (20) hours per week or an average of eighty (80) hours per month," and be paid for it. ([TN DHS SNAP Policy 24.27](https://www.tn.gov/content/dam/tn/human-services/documents/Policy%2024.27%20SNAP%20Students%20in%20Higher%20Educ.pdf))
- **Quitting wouldn't help you.** Your 10 hours don't count toward that exemption, but it's income, and it's one fewer thing you'd have to rely on. Quitting would also take away your own money.

**The student piece**
The same policy lists work-study as another path. It says the student "must be approved for work-study at the time of application for SNAP." You said you don't think you have a work-study job. Check with MTSU's financial aid office. If you don't have one, you could ask whether you could get one.

The policy page lists other exemptions as well. A caseworker can go through them with you, and it costs nothing to apply and ask.

**What I'd do next**
1. Check with MTSU financial aid about work-study, and ask whether anything else on the exemption list fits you.
2. Apply through [OneDHS](https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp?id=start_snap_application) or call 866-311-4287, and answer every question accurately.
3. Dial 211 if you want free help with the application.

I also found that you don't get SNAP, WIC, or TennCare now, so nothing changes in the screening. TennCare still looks unlikely, and WIC doesn't apply.

This is a screening, not a decision. Only the state agency decides, and anyone can apply.
